nodes.statement: From Proposition~6 in \cite{Val_Heun} (for parameters $m_1=0,m_2=1,m_3=0,m_0=0,A=2k^2,s=\frac{2k^2-1}{4},\sigma=2k^2-1$) we infer that \begin{equation} w_1(s):= \frac{k(w_+(s) - w_-(s))}{(w_+(0)+w_-(0))\cn(s,k)},\qquad w_2(s):= \frac{k(w_+(s) + w_-(s))}{(w_+(0)+w_-(0))\cn(s,k)} \end{equation} is a fundamental system of the ODE on each connected component of $\R\sm \{\cn(\cdot,k)=0\}$, which satisfies (i) thanks to $w_\pm(-s)=w_\mp(s)$.
nodes.statement_short: $w_1,w_2$ built from $w_\pm$ form a fundamental system with the right parity.

nodes.name: Items (ii)-(iv) from the product formula and the Wronskian
nodes.statement: The same proposition tells us that the product $w_+w_-$ is a real multiple of the function $1-k^2+(2k^2-1)\cn^2(\cdot,k)$ so that our choice for $w_1,w_2$ yields (ii). Differentiating this identity gives (iii) and (iv). Item (v) follows from the constancy of the Wronskian and $w_2(0)w_1'(0)-w_1(0)w_2'(0)= -k \sqrt{(1-k^2)(2k^2-1)}$.
nodes.statement_short: The product formula gives (ii), differentiation gives (iii),(iv) and the Wronskian gives (v).

nodes.name: Explicit smooth extensions $\hat w_1,\hat w_2$
nodes.statement: Finally, \eqref{eq:defn_w1w2_wavelike} shows that property (v) holds for the choice \begin{align*} \hat w_1(s) &:= \frac{k(w_+(s) - w_-(s))}{w_+(0)+w_-(0)} =\frac{k(\Theta_1(s+\alpha_k,k)e^{-s\zeta(\alpha_k,k)} - \Theta_1(s-\alpha_k,k)e^{s\zeta(\alpha_k,k)}}{ (w_+(0)+w_-(0))\Theta(s,k)}, \\ \hat w_2(s) &:= \frac{k(w_+(s) + w_-(s))}{w_+(0)+w_-(0)} = \frac{k(\Theta_1(s+\alpha_k,k)e^{-s\zeta(\alpha_k,k)} + \Theta_1(s-\alpha_k,k)e^{s\zeta(\alpha_k,k)}}{ (w_+(0)+w_-(0))\Theta(s,k)}, \end{align*} since $\zeta(\alpha_k,k)>0$ and $\Theta_1(\cdot,k),\Theta(\cdot,k)$ are positive periodic functions. Notice that the all complex zeros of $\Theta_1,\Theta$ are known to be non-real, see 1051.07 in \cite{ByrFri_handbook}. \qed
nodes.statement_short: The explicit $\hat w_j$ are smooth and positive since $\Theta,\Theta_1$ have no real zeros.

nodes.name: Proof of the properties of the angle function $\vartheta$ (wavelike)
nodes.statement: Now we prove Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_wavelike}. For $W_1,W_2,\vartheta$ as in \eqref{eq:def_Wj_wavelike},\eqref{eq:def_theta_wavelike} we have to prove that the following identities hold on $\R\sm\{\kappa=0\}$: $$ \vartheta' = \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|} \kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)},\quad \matII{W_1}{W_2}{W_1'}{W_2'} = \matII{0}{\frac{\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\kappa}}{-\frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa}{2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{ \frac{\mu\kappa'}{\kappa^2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}} \matII{\cosh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{\cosh(\vartheta)}. $$ \medskip We proceed as in the orbitlike case. With $c(s):= \frac{\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}}{\kappa(s)}$ we may write $$ \vecII{W_1(s)}{W_2(s)} = c(s) \vecII{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))}{\cosh(\vartheta(s))}. $$ Differentiating both sides and using Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_wavelike}~(ii),(iii) we arrive at \begin{align*} &-c(s)\vartheta'(s) \vecII{\cosh(\vartheta(s))}{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))} + c'(s) \vecII{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))}{\cosh(\vartheta(s))} \; =\; \vecII{W_1'(s)}{W_2'(s)} \\ &= \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{W_1(s)}{W_2(s)} - \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{W_2(s)}{W_1(s)} \\ &= \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)c(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))}{\cosh(\vartheta(s))} - \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa(s)^2c(s)}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{\cosh(\vartheta(s))}{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))}. \end{align*} This identity gives $$ \vartheta'(s) = \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)},\qquad c'(s) = \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)c(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} = \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)^2\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}} $$ and the claim follows from \begin{align*} \matII{W_1}{W_2}{W_1'}{W_2'} &= \matII{0}{c}{-c\vartheta'}{c'}\matII{\cosh(\vartheta)}{ -\sinh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{\cosh(\vartheta)}. \end{align*} \qed
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the hyperbolic polar representation $(W_1,W_2)=c(-\sinh\vartheta,\cosh\vartheta)$ and compare components.

nodes.name: Restate the identities to be proved
nodes.statement: Now we prove Proposition~\ref{prop:properties_vartheta_wavelike}. For $W_1,W_2,\vartheta$ as in \eqref{eq:def_Wj_wavelike},\eqref{eq:def_theta_wavelike} we have to prove that the following identities hold on $\R\sm\{\kappa=0\}$: $$ \vartheta' = \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|} \kappa^2}{2(\kappa^2-\mu)},\quad \matII{W_1}{W_2}{W_1'}{W_2'} = \matII{0}{\frac{\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}{\kappa}}{-\frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa}{2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}}{ \frac{\mu\kappa'}{\kappa^2\sqrt{\kappa^2-\mu}}} \matII{\cosh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{\cosh(\vartheta)}. $$
nodes.statement_short: State the wavelike formula for $\vartheta'$ and the hyperbolic matrix factorization.

nodes.name: Differentiate the hyperbolic polar representation
nodes.statement: We proceed as in the orbitlike case. With $c(s):= \frac{\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}}{\kappa(s)}$ we may write $$ \vecII{W_1(s)}{W_2(s)} = c(s) \vecII{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))}{\cosh(\vartheta(s))}. $$ Differentiating both sides and using Proposition~\ref{prop:W1W2_wavelike}~(ii),(iii) we arrive at \begin{align*} &-c(s)\vartheta'(s) \vecII{\cosh(\vartheta(s))}{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))} + c'(s) \vecII{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))}{\cosh(\vartheta(s))} \; =\; \vecII{W_1'(s)}{W_2'(s)} \\ &= \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{W_1(s)}{W_2(s)} - \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{W_2(s)}{W_1(s)} \\ &= \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)c(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))}{\cosh(\vartheta(s))} - \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa(s)^2c(s)}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} \vecII{\cosh(\vartheta(s))}{-\sinh(\vartheta(s))}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Substituting the $W_j'$-identities into the differentiated polar form.

nodes.name: Read off $\vartheta'$, $c'$ and conclude
nodes.statement: This identity gives $$ \vartheta'(s) = \frac{\sqrt{|\mu|}\kappa(s)^2}{2(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)},\qquad c'(s) = \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)c(s)}{\kappa(s)(\kappa(s)^2-\mu)} = \frac{\mu\kappa'(s)}{\kappa(s)^2\sqrt{\kappa(s)^2-\mu}} $$ and the claim follows from \begin{align*} \matII{W_1}{W_2}{W_1'}{W_2'} &= \matII{0}{c}{-c\vartheta'}{c'}\matII{\cosh(\vartheta)}{ -\sinh(\vartheta)}{-\sinh(\vartheta)}{\cosh(\vartheta)}. \end{align*} \qed
nodes.statement_short: Comparing components yields $\vartheta'$ and $c'$, hence the factorization.
